headline: Elon Musk has said Tesla is trimming the memory on its upcoming AI5 and AI6 chips, with the AI5 now set at 96GB, to make enough of them for its Optimus humanoid robot.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: Musk's posts date from about 1-2 Oct 2026, ten days before the window, and the 12 Oct pieces repeat them.
importance_line: It shows memory shortages shaping how many humanoid robots Tesla can build, which matters to buyers expecting Optimus robots and to Tesla's own production plans, but the claim that smaller memory will barely affect Optimus is Musk's own and untested.
summary: Not a Tesla App, a news site that covers Tesla, reports that Elon Musk said on X that Tesla cut the memory on its next in-house AI chips to build enough of them for Optimus, its humanoid robot, halving the AI5 to 72GB and trimming the AI6 by a third to 144GB, before raising the AI5 to 96GB so that Tesla would not be the only company using the smallest version of that memory type. Musk called the cut "the only way to get enough volume for Optimus production" and expects "a negligible effect on Optimus performance" because memory bandwidth, which is unchanged, limits these systems more than capacity does, while the outlet notes that memory maker Micron has estimated each humanoid robot may need about 200GB.
notes: Pool link (Global Sources relay) returned HTTP 429; the text read is Not a Tesla App's own article of 3 Oct 2026, which cites Musk's posts on X. Old news re-dated: Musk's posts date from about 1-2 Oct 2026 (Wccftech headlines).
